page: Vultr vcg-a16-6c-64g-16vram is a member of the Dedicated Metal GPU server family, featuring an Intel x86_64 architecture with 6 vCPUs across 3 physical cores. Each core supports 2 threads, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 10.67 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 350 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Although the GPU count is listed as 0.0, the platform integrates NVIDIA hardware components.

In benchmark evaluations, this server demonstrates highly specialized performance profiles. It achieves top-tier results in large language model (LLM) inference tasks, processing prompts at 8771.1 tokens per second for a small 135M model and 591.21 tokens per second for a medium 7B model, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Text generation speeds are also competitive, reaching 296.92 tokens per second on the 135M model. Conversely, general multi-threaded computational tasks show limitations; the bzip3 multi-threaded decompression benchmark scored 30.39 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25%. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks, including Passmark CPU (10693.5) and Redis SET operations (10.78 million operations per second), consistently fall within the average middle 50% range.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the vcg-a16-6c-64g-16vram is defined by its high memory density and specialized prompt processing capabilities relative to its moderate 6-vCPU compute allocation. This resource distribution makes it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that require rapid initial token processing but do not demand sustained multi-threaded CPU performance. Suitable workloads include small-to-medium scale LLM inference, database operations, memory-cached web serving, and general-purpose applications requiring a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio.
